## Why finance teams automate accounts payable


Manual accounts payable slows international teams down: invoices sit in inboxes, approvals wait on email, and month-end close depends on matching payments across several tools. Automating AP in one platform helps you pay vendors on time, keep a single view of spend, and reduce avoidable FX and operational cost. These are the gaps teams usually close first.


### Pay across borders and in local methods from one place


International invoices are now routine — software, legal, marketing, and imported goods. Many suppliers still invoice in USD or EUR, while local teams need to pay the way each market actually operates. In Brazil that often means Pix or boleto; in Mexico, SPEI or OXXO; in Colombia, local and global wallets. A single AP platform should let you send cross-border transfers and use those local methods without jumping between banks.


### Keep FX costs visible before you send


Currency swings can change the final cost of a supplier payment after the invoice is approved. You do not need a separate tool for every currency, but you do need to see the conversion and the fee before you confirm the payment, and to hold balances in the currencies you use most so you are not converting at the last minute.


### Control spend with limits, approvals, and scheduled payments


Automation is not only faster invoice capture. Finance teams can set spend limits, route approvals, store vendor details, and schedule payments for a future date — so departments move faster without giving up control. Corporate cards (physical or virtual) and invoice payments can live in the same workflow, which also simplifies reconciliation against statements and the general ledger.
